senses.gloss: to break through, make a breach, invade.
units: <cite ref="Pesachim 56a:10">Pes. 56ᵃ</cite> <he>פּוֹרְצִין פרצות וכ׳</he> made breaches in the fences of their gardens &c.; (Tosef. ib. II (III), 21 <he>פותחין גינותיהם וכ׳</he>); <cite ref="Menachot 71a:15">Men. 71ᵃ</cite>.

<cite ref="Berakhot 63a:25">Ber. 63ᵃ</cite> <he>כבר גדרת … יכול לִפְרוֹץ</he> having once fenced in, thou canst not tear down, i.e. having once approved, you cannot now find fault. Y. Snh. I, 19ᶜ top, v. <cite ref="Q00311"><he>פּוּץ</he></cite>.
<cite ref="Bereishit Rabbah 85:14">Gen. R. s. 85</cite> (ref. to <cite ref="Genesis 38:29">Gen. XXXVIII, 29</cite>) <he>כל הפּוֹרְצִים ממך וכ׳</he> all conquerors shall rise from thee (Judah).

<cite ref="Yalkut Shimoni on Nach 551:10">Yalk. Mic. 551</cite> <he>פָּרַצְתִּי גדרו של עולם מפני יעקב</he> I broke down the fence of the world (reversed the natural order of things) for the sake of Jacob (making his cattle extremely fecund); <he>ולע״ל אני פורץ אותו לבניו</he> and in the days to come I shall do so to his children.
<cite ref="Bava Kamma 60b:21">B. Kam. 60ᵇ</cite> <he>מלך פּוֹרֵץ … דרך</he> the king may break through fences to pave a way for his army.
<cite ref="Kohelet Rabbah 9:11:1">Koh. R. to IX, 11</cite> (ref. to <cite ref="Job 1:10">Job I, 10</cite>) <he>פ׳ גדרו של עולם וכ׳</he> his cattle reversed the order of things &c.

<cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Avodah Zarah 2:2:11">Y. Ab. Zar. II, 41ᵃ</cite> top <he>לא פָרַצְתָּ גדירן וכ׳</he> thou hast not torn down the fence of the scholars (not transgressed their law); <cite ref="Bereishit Rabbah 79">Gen. R. s. 79</cite>, v. <cite ref="C00213"><he>גָּדֵיר</he></cite>.

<cite ref="Vayikra Rabbah 26:2">Lev. R. s. 26</cite>, v. <cite ref="C00246"><he>גֶּדֶר</he> I</cite>; a. fr.—Part. pass. <he>פָּרוּץ</he>; f. <he>פְּרוּצָה</he>; pl. <he>פְּרוּצִים</he>, <cite ref="Q00842"><he>פְּרוּצִין</he></cite>; <he>פְּרוּצוֹת</he>.
<cite ref="Mishnah Kilayim 4:4">Kil. IV, 4</cite> <he>העומד מרובה על הפ׳</he> the unimpaired portion of the fence is larger than the ruined part, v. <cite ref="P00859"><he>עָמַד</he> II</cite>.

<cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Shabbat 10:2:3">Y. Sabb. X, 12ᶜ</cite> top <he>קופה פ׳</he> a bin which has been broken into (some of the contents of which has been taken); a. fr.—[<cite ref="Mishnah Peah 7:1">Peah VII, 1</cite> <he>בצד הפרוצה</he> Y. ed., v. <cite ref="Q01974"><he>פִּרְצָה</he></cite>.]
Y. Keth. I, 25ᵃ bot. שלא יִפְרְצוּ … בזימה in order that the daughters of Israel be not made heedless of chaste conduct (v. infra); a. e.—Part. pass. as ab. dissolute, bold.

<cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Ketubot 1:1:16">Ib.</cite> <he>מפני פ׳ אחד</he> because there might be one dissolute man (who may go to the expense of marriage for the sake of his gratification, with the intention of charging his bride with faithlessness afterwards).

<cite ref="Shir HaShirim Rabbah 4:12:1">Cant. R. to IV, 12</cite> <he>לא נמצא בהן אחד פ׳ בעיוה</he> not one of them was of immoral conduct; <cite ref="Vayikra Rabbah 32">Lev. R. s. 32</cite> <he>פְּרוּץ ערוה</he>.
<cite ref="Gittin 46a:2">Gitt. 46ᵃ</cite> <he>שלא יהו בנות … פ׳ וכ׳</he> that the daughters of Israel may not be loose in moral conduct or in vows (v. supra).
<cite ref="Bereishit Rabbah 70">Gen. R. s. 70</cite> (ref. to <cite ref="Genesis 29:21">Gen. XXIX, 21</cite>) <he>אפי׳ אדם פ׳ אינו וכ׳</he> even the most shameless man would not use such language.
<cite ref="Sotah 7a:6">Sot. 7ᵃ</cite> <he>אבל פ׳</he> but if they are known to be of dissolute habits, opp. <he>כשרין</he>.
<cite ref="Ketubot 2b:14">Keth. 2ᵇ</cite>, sq. <he>משום פ׳</he> on account of loose women, opp. <he>צנועות</he>; a. fr.

<cite ref="Shabbat 13a">Sabb. 13ᵃ</cite>; <cite ref="Tosefta Shabbat 1:14">Tosef. ib. I, 14</cite> <he>עד היכן פָּרְצָה טהרה וכ׳</he> how far the observance of levitical cleanness has spread in Israel!; a. e.
<cite ref="Tosefta Kilaim 3:3">Tosef. Kil. III, 3</cite> <he>מחיצת הכרם שנִפְרְצָה</he> if the partition of a vineyard has come down; <he>גדרה ונ׳</he> if he repaired it, and it came down again.
<cite ref="Mishnah Eruvin 9:2">Erub. IX, 2</cite> <he>חצר גדולה שנפרצה לקטנה</he> if the partition between a large court and a smaller one has been broken into.

<cite ref="Yalkut Shimoni on Nach 352">Yalk. Ez. 352</cite> a good shepherd <he>שנ׳ גדר צאנו</he> the fold of whose flock was broken into; (Ruth R. introd. <he>שנפלה</he>). <cite ref="C00246"><he>גדר</he></cite> Tanḥ. Bal. 13 <he>ראה שישראל נִפְרָצִים שם</he> he (Balak) saw that the Israelites would be broken into (sustain a great loss) there; <cite ref="Bamidbar Rabbah 20:19">Num. R. s. 20</cite> <he>שיש פרצים</he> (corr. acc.).
<cite ref="Avot D'Rabbi Natan 5:2">Ab. d’R. N. ch. V</cite> <he>ונִפְרְצוּ וכ׳</he>, v. <cite ref="Q01974"><he>פִּרְצָה</he></cite>; a. fr.

senses.gloss: to be unrestrained, dissolute. Tanḥ. Vayera 9 לפי שנפרצו מעשיהם בזנות because their doings were unrestrained in matters of sexual morality; a. e.

units: <cite ref="Bereishit Rabbah 73">Gen. R. s. 73</cite> (ref. to <cite ref="Genesis 30:43">Gen. XXX, 43</cite>) <he>נִפְרְצָה לו פרצה מעין וכ׳</he> an (abnormal) increase of wealth was granted to him similar to that expected in the days to come (v. Yalk. Mic. l. c.); <cite ref="Yalkut Shimoni on Torah 130">Yalk. Gen. 130</cite>; <cite ref="Yalkut Shimoni on Nach 989">Yalk. Koh. 989</cite>; a. e.
<cite ref="Mishnah Sukkah 3:1">Succ. III, 1</cite> <he>נפרצו עליו</he> if its leaves are severed (and only kept together by a band), v. <cite ref="Q01572"><he>פָּרַד</he></cite>.

senses.gloss: (denom. of פָּרִיץ) to be defiant. Tosef. Macc. V (IV), 13 אפי׳ עומד ומַפְרִיץ וכ׳ even if he stands up defiantly (saying, he did not mind more lashes), you dare not add &c.

to become dissolute, be unrestrained, licentious. Y. Sabb. III, 6ᵃ bot. שלא תִתְפָּרֵץ that she may not assume immoral habits; ib. שלא יִתְפָּרְצוּ that people may not be unrestrained; Y. Bets. II, 61ᶜ
